subject: Post-call: pilot smoke tests & reserved capacity sizing for Ledgerly
messages:
From: Ellen Park <ellen.park@ledgerly.com>
To: Markus Klein <markus.klein@redwood.ai>, Camila Reyes <camila.reyes@redwood.ai>
Cc: ops@ledgerly.com
Date: Sat, 20 Mar 2027 15:12:00 -0700
Subject: Dedicated capacity: performance baseline and goals

Thanks again for the call earlier — good alignment. I pulled together the things we promised to share: a short sample of production queries (anonymized), the percent of streaming vs non-streaming calls, and our rough concurrency profile. Attached: initial_workload_samples.json.

High-level goals from our side (what we'd like to validate in the pilot):
- Streaming chat p95 latency target: <= 250ms for aggregate responses (we understand some variance for long context).
- Non-streaming batch generation p95: <= 350ms for inference-only path.
- Sustained concurrency: 80–120 simultaneous user sessions (concurrent inferences), with occasional spikes to 220 for <10m windows.
- Throughput: expected ~55k tokens/minute at peak.
- Max acceptable cold-start: 1.2s to first byte for a pinned model variant.

Questions for Redwood:
1) What reserved throughput (tokens/s or concurrency) should we commit to for a pilot that proves these SLOs?
2) Which GPU family would you recommend for predictable streaming latency under this workload (we mentioned H100 and A100 on the call)?
3) Any suggested smoke tests we should run before the kickoff?

Next steps from our side: confirm the pilot window (we were thinking Mar 29–Apr 5) and share API keys for sandbox.

Thanks,
Ellen Park
Director of Platform Engineering, Ledgerly

From: Markus Klein <markus.klein@redwood.ai>

Subject: Re: Dedicated capacity: performance baseline and goals

Appreciate the samples and clear goals, Ellen — this is great and actionable. Summary of what we'll do and an initial proposal: 

1) Pilot sizing and reserved throughput recommendation (quick answer):
- Start pilot on a 3-GPU reserved pool. Recommended cards: 2x H100 (for streaming p95 headroom) + 1x A100 80GB as a cost tradeoff node for heavy batching. This mix gives us predictable latency for streaming while retaining good batching efficiency for non-streaming bursts.
- Map to throughput: we expect this pool to cover ~100 concurrent streaming sessions steady-state, and absorb spikes up to 220 with short autoscale headroom.

2) Smoke tests (what we'll run before kickoff):
- End-to-end streaming latency burn (30m sustained window) using your sample traces (we'll replay streaming frames at the same inter-arrival times).
- Concurrency soak: ramp to 120 concurrent streams for 15 minutes, then spike to 220 for 5 minutes — verify p95s and tail behavior.
- Cold-start measurements: tear down a worker and measure TTFB for pinned model variants.
- Token throughput verification for batch path (tokens/min measurement).

3) Deliverables and cadence:
- We'll deliver a brief benchmark plan (attached: redwood_benchmark_plan.xlsx) with exact steps + scripts + expected success criteria.
- Ben will own the pilot execution; Camila will coordinate infra/permissions and any private deployment needs.

4) Timeline:
- Agree pilot window Mar 29–Apr 5. We propose to run smoke tests on Mar 27–28 (dry run) and start pilot on Mar 29.

Open items:
- Ellen: confirm that Ledgerly can provide a sandbox API key and a small test dataset with streaming markers by Mar 24.
- We will also need a target SLO acceptance matrix (pass/fail thresholds) from you so our telemetry can gate success.

Thanks — I'll loop Ben and Camila into the technical kickoff thread.

— Markus
Head of Solutions, Redwood Inference

Subject: GPU matrix + quick perf notes for Ledgerly pilot

Folks — quick tech note to support Markus' recommendation. I ran ballpark numbers against a benchmark harness yesterday (using Ledgerly sample shapes):

- H100 (2x in pool): streaming p95 ~ 180–220ms at 90 concurrent sessions (depending on prompt length). Sustained tokens/sec ~ 1,200–1,400 per card in our setup.
- A100 80GB (1x): optimized for batching; when we route non-streaming batch requests here we see batch throughput improvements of ~1.6x vs H100 at 512-token windows.
- L4 (cost-optimized): we can use for low-priority workloads but tail latency becomes unpredictable under bursty user traffic — not recommended for primary streaming SLOs.

Pilot orchestration notes:
- Reserved throughput: we'll express as both tokens/sec (1200 tokens/s steady) + concurrency slot reservations (100 streaming slots). This lets us do deterministic admission control and graceful degradation.
- KV cache warmup: replays should include realistic user session prefixes — cold caches increase p95 by ~45–70ms on H100 in our runs. We'll measure and report cold vs warm numbers in final report.

I'll prepare the GPU throughput CSV and upload to the shared Drive (link below) and include the benchmark commands so Ledgerly can reproduce.

Ben
Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
